covers.quote: Question marks usually go after the last letter in a sentence
Like other punctuation marks, question marks stay with the text they refer to.

rules.quote: Usually, this is immediately after the last letter of the last word of the sentence.
rules.violation_condition: a question mark placed with a preceding space before it rather than immediately after the last letter of the sentence or enclosed text
when: unless brackets or quotation marks dictate its relative placement
rules.why: G-1, G-4: The heading and first sentence state the general placement of question marks immediately following the text.

covers.quote: For brackets and quotation marks, place the question mark:

examples.note: Question mark inside quotation marks because the question is the quoted text.

parts.quote: She asked, ‘Is the report due on Tuesday?’

examples.note: Question mark inside parentheses because the question is the parenthetical text.

parts.quote: They decided (and why wouldn’t they?) to cancel the program.

rules.quote: before a closing bracket or quotation mark if the question is part of the text in the brackets or quotation marks
rules.violation_condition: a question mark placed outside a closing bracket or quotation mark when the question belongs to the enclosed text
when: the question is part of the text in the brackets or quotation marks
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Specific positioning rule for question marks inside brackets/quotes.

examples.note: Question mark outside quotation mark because the surrounding sentence is the question.

parts.quote: What did she mean by ‘the report is due ASAP’?

examples.note: Question mark outside bracket because the surrounding sentence is the question.

parts.quote: Did they decide to cancel the program (the EDTA program)?

rules.quote: after the closing bracket or quotation mark if the question is part of the surrounding text.
rules.violation_condition: a question mark placed inside a closing bracket or quotation mark when the question belongs to the surrounding sentence
when: the question is part of the surrounding text
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Specific positioning rule for question marks outside brackets/quotes.
